newsitem.title: USA: PEMEX sees Yankee bond early '97, oil output 3mbpd.
newsitem.headline: PEMEX sees Yankee bond early '97, oil output 3mbpd.

text.p: Mexico's state oil company Petroleos Mexicanos (PEMEX) hopes to issue a "Yankee" bond by the end of the first quarter 1997, a senior company finance official said Wednesday.

Alfredo Mrquez, associate managing director of finance at PEMEX, estimated the country would offer around $300-$500 million on the U.S. Yankee bond market and said its launch "ideally should be very near the end of the first quarter."

He said that PEMEX still expects oil output next year to top three million barrels a day (bpd), rising by 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 200,000 bpd from a three-year high 2.883 million barrels a day expected in the fourth quarter of 1996.
"We think we will see increasing production on average 150,000 or as much as 200,000 bpd (next year)," Mrquez said.
At the end of October, PEMEX chairman Adrian Lajous said that the company's expansion plans for 1997 included rises in refinery, natural gas and petrochemical spending.
PEMEX officials said last month they expected to issue $900 million of external debt in 1997, half of which would come from the Yankee market.
